findings.message: deleteItem calls setActivities from inside the setItems updater function, so the side effect runs once for every time React invokes the updater. main.tsx wraps the app in <StrictMode>. In development React calls state updater functions twice, so deleting one item adds two identical 'removed' entries (with different UUIDs) to Recent Activity. Calling setState during another updater is also unsupported and can warn. Read the item from the current `items` (or a ref) and call setItems and setActivities one after the other.

updateItem, now hooked up to the Edit modal, never adds an activity entry, even though ActivityEntry.action includes 'updated' and 'restocked' and add/delete both log one. A user edits an item, e.g. changing its quantity from 2 to 50. The table updates, but the dashboard's Recent Activity shows nothing, so the change is missing from the audit trail while adds and deletes do show up.
